subject: FluxData POC — performance acceptance & responsibilities
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood-inference.com>
To: Priya Sinha <priya.s@fluxdata.com>, Daniel Ortiz <daniel.ortiz@fluxdata.com>
Cc: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood-inference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Sep 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: FluxData POC — performance acceptance & responsibilities

Thanks again for the call earlier, Priya/Daniel — good discussion and appreciate the clear use case details. Per request, here's a concise post-call recap and the proposed acceptance criteria + owners for the trial so we can get the technical kickoff scheduled.

High-level POC scope
- Inference serving of FluxData's summarization pipeline using Redwood-hosted trial instance (private model variant we discussed).
- Evaluate performance (latency/throughput), token economics, and output quality on a 2k-document representative sample you agreed to provide.

Proposed acceptance KPIs (we should agree these before kickoff)
1) Latency (inference server end-to-end, cold-start excluded)
   - p50 <= 120 ms per request
   - p95 <= 350 ms per request
2) Throughput
   - Sustained 600 requests / minute (95% of test window) with average concurrency of 8 sessions
3) Cost per token
   - Average inference cost <= $0.0009 per token (target) across the sample workload
4) Quality / correctness
   - Automated metrics: ROUGE-L F1 >= 0.68 on the provided eval set
   - Human spot-check: no more than 2% hallucination rate in a 200-sample audit
5) Stability
   - No critical errors (500s) during the test window; SLO for request success >= 99.5%

Ownership (suggested)
- Sean (me): POC executive owner — timelines, contract/SOW signoff, commercial questions
- Ava: Technical lead — test harness, eval automation, data ingestion, and live-run monitoring
- Laura: Customer success / sign-off — coordinate feedback sessions, quality review, acceptance checklist

Timeline (proposed)
- Sep 14 — baseline environment provisioned; we push initial config and credentials
- Sep 15–22 — ingest sample corpus, run smoke tests, iterate on prompt/temperature settings
- Sep 23–29 — full evaluation runs (automated + human audit)
- Oct 1 — results review and acceptance decision

Immediate next steps
1) Priya/Daniel: confirm sample dataset delivery by Sep 13 and list any redaction constraints.
2) Priya: sign the attached SOW draft (we can DocuSign or we can mirror your PO flow).
3) Ava: will send the test harness repo and quickstart guide (attached) by EOD 9/8.
4) Schedule 30-min technical kickoff for Sep 14 — please indicate availability.

Attachments included: redwood-poc-quickstart.pdf, sow-draft.docx, fluxdata-sample-queries.json

--
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood-inference.com | +1 415-555-0123

From: Priya Sinha <priya.s@fluxdata.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Daniel Ortiz <daniel.ortiz@fluxdata.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Sep 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FluxData POC — performance acceptance & responsibilities

Thanks Sean — that breakdown is helpful. A few clarifications from our side so we can align: 

- Dataset: we'll deliver the 2k-document export and an additional 200-document audit set by COB Sep 13. Files will include sensitive customer IDs; we need a confirmation on data handling and retention (are you able to auto-delete after 90 days?).
- Latency measure: can you confirm whether latency targets are measured per text chunk request or per end-to-end summarization job? Our jobs typically chunk at 512 tokens and then stitch summaries — prefer to measure per overall job.
- Cost per token: flux uses tokens ~ 1.2x estimated due to pre-processing footprint. Can we include a +/- 10% buffer on the cost KPI for the first run?

Also, on signoff: our PM (CC'd) will want a short checklist that includes: data retention policy, export of audit logs, and plan for model fallback if SLOs are missed in production.

If you can confirm the retention and the latency measurement definition by tomorrow, we'll proceed with dataset delivery.

Best,
Priya
Head of Data Products | FluxData
priya.s@fluxdata.com

From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood-inference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood-inference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Sep 2026 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FluxData POC — performance acceptance & responsibilities

Looping in technical details and our proposed measurement plan (so Sean can push to Priya):

Measurement definitions (we'll instrument these in the harness)
- "Request" vs "Job": we'll measure both.
   - Request = single model invocation (one chunk).
   - Job = end-to-end pipeline per document (all chunks + stitch time).
- Latency KPIs: we'll report job-level p50/p95 (this matches Flux's requirement) and also per-request metrics for debugging.
- Throughput: measured as completed jobs per minute over a rolling 5-min window; we'll record concurrency and queue lengths.
- Cost/token: estimated by actual GPU-seconds * hardware unit cost + amortized infra; we'll provide an itemized cost log so Flux can map to their accounting.
- Quality: automated ROUGE and a 200-sample human audit; QA team will tag hallucinations and false facts.

Test harness & artifacts
- I will upload a test harness repo link and a small Dockerized runner for the trial. It will produce: metrics.csv, transcripts/, and a human-audit sheet.
- We'll add a retention flag: data in the trial workspace will be auto-deleted after 90 days unless Flux requests export. We'll also provide audit logs export within 48 hours on request.

Owners (technical)
- Ava: test harness authoring, monitoring dashboards, cost calc exports
- Sean: commercial approvals and scheduling
- Laura: coordinate human-audit panel and acceptance signoff

I'll prepare a one-page acceptance checklist that matches your PM asks and share by EOD today. Once Priya confirms dataset drop and retention terms we'll schedule the Sep 14 kickoff.

- Ava
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ava.chen@redwood-inference.com

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood-inference.com>

Date: Wed, 9 Sep 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FluxData POC — performance acceptance & responsibilities

Thanks Priya — quick confirmations: 
- Retention: Redwood will auto-delete trial workspace data after 90 days; we will also provide an export of logs and results on request before deletion. I'll attach a short data handling addendum for signatures.
- Latency KPI: we'll use job-level p50/p95 as the primary acceptance metric (per Ava's note) and include per-request as diagnostic data.
- Cost tolerance: agree to a first-run buffer of +/- 10% on the cost per token KPI; we'll mark this as "informational" on run 1 and re-evaluate on the production plan.

Next: Priya — once you drop the dataset (by Sep 13), we'll lock the kickoff for Sep 14 at 10:00 AM PT unless you propose another time. I'm attaching the SOW draft and the quickstart. If those look good, I can send a DocuSign route for signatures.

Cheers,
Sean
